related_questions.question: What is the IRS 8938 filing requirement?
related_questions.snippet: If you live in the United States, you must file if your specified foreign assets are worth over $50,000 ($100,000 for joint filers) at the end of the tax year or over $75,000 ($150,000 for joint filers) at any point during the tax year.

related_questions.question: Do I have to file both form 8938 and FBAR?
related_questions.snippet: The filing of Form 8938 does not relieve you of the separate requirement to file the FBAR if you are otherwise required to do so, and vice-versa. Depending on your situation, you may be required to file Form 8938 or the FBAR or both forms, and certain foreign accounts may be required to be reported on both forms.

related_questions.question: What happens if I have more than $100,000 in a foreign bank account?
related_questions.snippet: Under the Bank Secrecy Act, U.S. taxpayers must report their overseas bank accounts and financial assets, even if those assets do not generate taxable income. You must report any account with more than $10,000, or if your combined accounts have a total value greater than $10,000.

related_questions.question: What is the value threshold for 8938?
related_questions.snippet: Single or Married Filing Separately: You must file Form 8938 if the total value of your foreign assets is greater than $50,000 on the last day of the tax year or more than $75,000 at any point during the year.
